evidence.annotationMethod: Assistant visual interpretation of original images; approximate frame corners, not automated detections. Coordinates retained for review.

interpretation: Two-storey front bay, with lower-ground window visible in entrance photo.
Two-storey rear wing, followed by a lower rear extension.
Rooflight and rear glazed doors visible in extension interior.
No attic floor appears on supplied plan; rear dormers may belong to neighbours and are not added.
plan.confidence: Printed dimensions used as soft constraints; plan pixels are schematic, not an exact survey.

depth.reason: Published inference requires Linux/CUDA; this host is macOS ARM with no CUDA GPU.
depth.parameterization: Default Log-stage2 is affine-invariant log depth, not metres. Align in log-depth space with independent metric anchors.

uncertainties: Rear elevation attribution needs review: adjoining houses overlap in both rear photographs.
Basement depth and rear ground levels are not surveyed.
Side windows, rear opening sizes and rooflight dimensions have not been numerically fitted.
No monocular depth was generated or used.

provenance.method: Assistant-authored semantic hypotheses and pixel observations; SciPy bounded robust least-squares fitting. No depth inference.
provenance.selection: Lowest training objective among the two rear roof hypotheses; check-image window residuals excluded from objective.
limitations: Rear elevation attribution needs review: adjoining houses overlap in both rear photographs.
Basement depth and rear ground levels are not surveyed.
Side windows, rear opening sizes and rooflight dimensions have not been numerically fitted.
No monocular depth was generated or used.
Rectangular opening envelopes approximate arched frames.
Each roof section is a closed derived shell; overlapping construction joints are not a fabrication-ready CSG model.
The plan defines a basement but its floor elevation remains assumed.
Four photo observations share repeated facade geometry; this is a prototype fit, not a surveyed model.
